scope: The implemented success coordinate agrees with the signed reciprocal on regular bins. The decoded phase distance bounds the relative error even across a sign change.

The exact sine clock on either spectral sign has squared relative error of order 1/(dM)² for any superposition. For a normalized input the selected branch has mass at least 4d² and normalized vector error at most 160/(dM), preserved by unitary uncomputation.

The inverse Fourier transform, controlled-time phases and sine-state preparation give the exact eigenphase kernel. Their adjoint uncomputes the reciprocal-weighted state to a zero clock. The signed solution branch has probability at least 4d² and normalized error at most 160/(dM).
The initialized sine-envelope clock has unit norm and is prepared by a unitary.
The controlled-time phases and quantum Fourier transform are unitary.
